title: Chapter 66: Build Her a Park
html:
“How can I help?” the man asked softly, his manner surprisingly free of businesslike formality.

“Director Luo, this is Xiao Chen, the brave young man who helped the police capture the fugitive.” Uncle Xu drew Chen Ge forward. “He’s here about the request I mentioned earlier. He wants to rent the unused underground parking lot.”

“I see. Leave us for a moment. You can get back to work.” Director Luo motioned for Uncle Xu to go.

Director Luo invited Chen Ge to sit on the sofa and poured two cups of tea. “I’m told you wish to rent the underground parking lot. May I ask what you plan to do with it?”

“I wish to expand the Haunted House. I want to build an underground maze inside the parking lot.”

“An underground maze. Not a bad idea, but do you have the money and the ability to manage something on that scale? The rent will be trivial compared with the cost of fitting out the space.” Director Luo leaned back on the sofa, fatigue clouding his eyes. “I’m not opposed to the idea, and I can rent you the lot, but first I need to ask you a few questions.”

Although Director Luo had agreed in principle, he had not named a price, so Chen Ge remained nervous. “Go ahead.”

“You own a Haunted House, so you know better than I do how much it costs to start one. If a hotel fails, its tables, chairs, and equipment can be sold or reused. If your Haunted House fails, what will you do with all those specialized props?”

It was a valid concern, one Chen Ge had never considered.

“Even if you revive the Haunted House, how will you attract repeat customers? A Haunted House is usually a one-time experience. The initial excitement will fade, and your pool of potential customers is finite. You’re planning a major investment. Are you certain you’ll recover it?

“One last question. If you build the Haunted House underground, how will you promote it? Your attendance depends heavily on the park’s. How will the Haunted House survive when the park closes?”

Chen Ge knew Director Luo meant well. Everyone advising him not to invest in the Haunted House had his best interests at heart.

Director Luo’s three questions circled through Chen Ge’s mind. The black phone solved the first two, leaving only the third. If New Century Park closed, his Haunted House would naturally close with it.

Relocating would be difficult; the paperwork alone would be a nightmare. Worse, his limited budget made finding another site large enough for the black phone’s scenarios all but impossible.

“Have you seriously considered those questions?” Director Luo seemed to anticipate his answer. “Why don’t you go home for now? We mustn’t rush into an important decision without careful research and thought.”

Chen Ge sat unmoved on the couch. He turned to look at Director Luo and asked directly, “Is the park really going to close soon?”

Director Luo did not confirm or deny, but the tiredness in his eyes deepened. “If I say the park is really closing soon, will you insist on renting the underground parking lot?”

“I will.” Chen Ge’s answer surprised Director Luo. “Director Luo, I already have the solution for your first and second questions. And your third question is not valid.”

Fire danced in Chen Ge’s eyes as he pressed on fearlessly. “My Haunted House has never relied on anyone else, and its attendance won’t always depend on the park. Give me time, and I’ll not only draw countless visitors to the Haunted House—I’ll use it to revive the entire park! Renting the underground lot is only the beginning. I plan to build the world’s first theme park devoted entirely to horror.”

Only after finishing did Chen Ge remember Uncle Xu’s advice: the less you said, the fewer mistakes you made.

He regarded Director Luo uncertainly, already regretting how much he had revealed.

Director Luo set down his cup, the weariness gone from his eyes. After a moment of silence, he laughed. “You remind me of myself when I was young.”

He stood and drew back the curtains, revealing the entire park beyond the office windows.

“No one is more devastated by the thought of New Century Park closing, or more reluctant to let it go.” He opened the window, letting the wind ruffle his graying hair. “This park means the world to me. If I could, I would keep it open forever.”

Director Luo turned to Chen Ge with a complicated smile—the calm expression of a man who had seen fortunes rise and fall and accepted the vagaries of fate. “I’ve heard your story. After your parents disappeared, you left your job to take over their Haunted House. In some ways, our stories are very similar, but you’re luckier than I was.”

He picked up the room’s only framed photograph. It showed a father and daughter. The father was of average height with a gentle demeanor. The little girl in his arms was adorable, but her hands bent at painful angles, and her eyes held no spark of life.

“This is my daughter. She suffered from severe aphasia and needed a special brace just to stand. God was cruel to her, but she was a strong little girl who loved to smile—at me and at the world.” Director Luo gazed through the window at the sky. “But the world never smiled back. I used to take her for walks in the garden, but none of the other children would play with her. Whenever she looked helplessly at me, I knew she was afraid she had done something wrong, that she was to blame for being shunned. I didn’t know how to comfort her, so eventually we took her out only on rainy days, when she wouldn’t have to face the indifferent crowds. Perhaps that was when I first dreamed of building my daughter a theme park of her own.

“Unfortunately, she didn’t live to see the park open.” Director Luo set down the frame, his eyes still surprisingly calm. “Many people don’t understand why I would risk bankruptcy to keep an outdated theme park alive, but I believe you might.”

“I do.” Chen Ge had already stood up earlier. He had not expected that Director Luo would reveal such intimate information to him.

“Everyone is trying to find a way out, but you’re different. You’ve surprised me.” After closing the window, Director Luo pulled out a document from his drawer. “Actually, when Uncle Xu came to me with your request, I had already approved it. Take it. Come to me if you need any help, but remember, you only have two to three months left.”
